methods.name: Stage-Progression

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.0B - $2.3B.

private.name: Exotec
private.rationale: Same sector (Robotics & Manufacturing), same stage (Series D), post-money $2B

data.narrative:
Outrider, a Series D robotics and manufacturing automation company that has raised $262M to date, was valued through triangulation against a comp universe of 9 private and 1 public peer company. The private peer set includes same-sector and same/adjacent-stage firms: Exotec (Series D, $2.0B), Divergent (Series E, $2.3B), Hadrian (Series C, $1.6B), and Nimble Robotics (Series C, $1.0B).

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $262M total raised as a base proxy and applying a 1.5x multiplier typical for Series D progression, yields $393M. Peer-median benchmarking across the four comparable companies produces an $1.8B implied valuation, with a range spanning $1.0B to $2.3B. The midpoint of these two methods—$1.1B—sits substantially above the stage-progression result but well within the peer distribution.

This analysis supports a valuation range of $334M (low) to $2.1B (high), with a median estimate of $1.1B. The wide dispersion reflects meaningful uncertainty around stage maturity and capital efficiency relative to peers. The peer-median method carries greater weight given Outrider's operational proximity to the comparable set, though the stage-progression floor provides a conservative anchor. Key uncertainties include revenue scale, gross margin profile, and customer concentration relative to the peer group.
